title: Morphogenesis should be trainable by reinforcement for specific anatomical outcomes

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Morphogenesis should be trainable by reinforcement for specific anatomical outcomes

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: TAME predicts (not yet tested) that the collective intelligence of tissues may be trainable by reinforcement learning, using rewards and punishments such as nutrients, endorphins or shock, to produce specific morphological or gene-expression outcomes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2022, Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds › Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Not Just Philosophy: Why These Parallels Matter

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Another key prediction that remains to be tested (ongoing in our lab) is trainability of morphogenesis. The collective intelligence of tissues could be sophisticated enough to be trainable via reinforcement learning for specific morphological outcomes.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Technological Approach to Mind Everywhere: An Experimentally-Grounded Framework for Understanding Diverse Bodies and Minds”, Frontiers in systems neuroscience (2022), doi:10.3389/fnsys.2022.768201; section “Somatic Cognition: An Example of Unconventional Agency in Detail › Not Just Philosophy: Why These Parallels Matter”. Scope: Regenerating or developing animal tissues; clinical settings

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2022-tame-20: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.38

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A controlled reinforcement-learning assay could clearly test the prediction. The required training histories and morphological readouts are not available in existing public datasets, so new experiments are necessary.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Repeatedly pair tissue states or actions with prespecified rewards or punishments, then test on held-out conditions whether morphology or expression shifts toward a rewarded target more than yoked and unpaired controls.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Distinguishing learning from selection or toxicity requires new controls.

The paper explicitly describes the prediction as untested.

Public datasets do not appear to contain reinforcement schedules with longitudinal anatomical outcomes.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.72
data existence: 0.12
analysis feasibility: 0.3
data adequacy: 0.08

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A reinforcement test with yoked controls would cleanly confirm or refute trainability of a morphological outcome. The source paper marks the experiment as not yet done, and public follow-up through 2026 is proposal and framework rather than a deposited training result. The necessary measurements are still to be collected.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Deliver a nutrient, endorphin, or shock contingency contingent on an anatomical or expression state, against a yoked non-contingent control; trainability holds if only the contingent group moves toward the rewarded morphology.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Later discussions and proposed reinforcement protocols have not released such an outcome dataset.

No public experiment pairs contingent reward or punishment with a morphological endpoint.
